identityDecision: Use the named Gjellestad ship-grave archaeological point as the primary anchor and the surviving Jellhaugen mound geometry as a secondary anchor in the same landscape record.

archaeologicalScope.finding: Georadar identified the ship grave in 2018 together with multiple burial mounds and Iron Age buildings. The approximately 20-metre imprint lay just below the topsoil and was excavated in 2020–2021.
archaeologicalScope.landscapeDistinction: Store norske leksikon identifies Jellhaugen as the large surviving mound and the ship grave as one of the destroyed mounds in the surrounding cemetery.

crossChecks.finding: The surviving mound is approximately 85 by 70 metres and up to nine metres high; it is a separate monument from the Gjellestad ship grave.
The fragile ship remains are still located at the findspot and are monitored with temperature and moisture sensors.

rejectedCandidates.reason: Remote uncontracted point east of both archaeological anchors.

rejectedCandidates.name: Jellhaugen
rejectedCandidates.reason: Valid secondary anchor, but not the mound that contained the Gjellestad ship.
A broad farm or locality point does not identify either archaeological monument.
The full burial, settlement and ritual landscape has no captured verified canonical geometry in this production.

radiusDecision.covers: The ship grave, Jellhaugen and the immediate connecting part of Viksletta for gameplay.
doesNotRepresent: a legal protection or security zone
